messages:
ajay: Overnight nightly-run flagged a large quality drop on the summarizer promptset after we flipped to the new FP8 profile for llama3-v2. Delta ~6.2% acc drop. Screenshot + short examples attached. Can @kaelyn or @maria take a quick look?
kaelyn: Ugh. saw the alert. do you have the delta table or the exact metric that regressed?
ajay: Pasted top-line numbers below (baseline -> new):
```
ROUGE-L: 0.881 -> 0.823  (-6.6%)
BLEU   : 0.412 -> 0.386  (-6.3%)
QA-F1  : 0.742 -> 0.695  (-6.3%)
```
ajay: Also attaching one raw gen that went bad (extra hallucinated sentence).
maria: Did we change the calibration routine for FP8 or switch quant params?
ajay: Yes — recent PR upstream changed per-channel scale estimation and added a small clamp on zero_point for stability. PR: github.com/redwood/infra/PR/452. That ran in nightly with the FP8 profile.
jonah: Can we repro with INT8 profile (same calib) to check if it's FP8-specific or general quantization sensitivity?
ajay: Good call. I queued three runs: (1) current FP8+new-calib, (2) FP8+old-calib, (3) INT8+new-calib. Eval-bot should post results shortly.
eval-bot: Run queued -> id rq_1979004321_1. Running on eval-pool-3. Params: model=llama3-v2, set=summarizer-nightly, seeds=[42,73], profiles=[fp8_new,fp8_old,int8_new].
ops-bot: Notifying dedicated-ci that this is higher priority.
eval-bot: Run complete. Results: fp8_new=0.823, fp8_old=0.878, int8_new=0.869. Full CSV: https://artifacts.internal/runs/rq_1979004321_1/results.csv
ajay: fp8_old restores almost all quality. So regression points to the new calibration change, not FP8 arithmetic itself.
kaelyn: Ok that narrows it. Which step in calib changed? per-channel scale estimation vs clipping heuristics?
ajay: Per-channel scale calc changed (we now estimate scale per-output-channel using L2-norm instead of max-abs), and we added a zero_point clamp to avoid extreme offsets for tiny activations.
maria: Can we try: old scale + new clamp and new scale + old clamp to isolate? Small A/B helps.
jonah: Also request to run with eval prompt seeds that produced hallucinations to inspect activations and KV stats. Might be a rare corner.
ajay: Will queue micro-sweeps: combinations (scale_method={maxabs,l2}, clamp={on,off}) across 10 seeds.
eval-bot: Micro-sweep queued -> id rq_1979004321_2. ETA ~15m.
eval-bot: Micro-sweep done. Quick summary: combos with l2 scale + clamp=on show the worst drop. l2+clamp=off almost identical to baseline. Table: l2/on=0.821, l2/off=0.876, maxabs/on=0.874, maxabs/off=0.875.
kaelyn: Strong signal: the clamp interacting with l2 scale is the culprit. Maybe l2 gives tiny scales for some channels so clamp pushes zero_point far and that perturbs dequantization.
maria: For safety, proposal: revert to previous calibration in the nightly pipeline while we patch clamp logic. Create canary that applies l2 scale only where per-channel variance > threshold.
ajay: Agreed. I'll open a revert PR for nightly profile and a follow-up with a safe clamp rule.
jonah: Also add an eval regression check that flags >2% drop post-calib-change per promptset so we catch this earlier.
kaelyn: Good. assign tasks?
ajay: I'll do the revert PR and the canary plan. @maria please own the clamp fix and tests. @jonah add the extra regression gate to nightly. I'll draft the incident note if we need to notify customers.
maria: on it. starting a small unit test with synthetic channels to cover edge-case zero_point.
ajay: Thanks. Filing a short postmortem if revert doesn't fully fix. :thumbsup:
